name: Tectonic Shear Gauntlet
description:
The Tectonic Shear Gauntlet is a powered combat gauntlet developed by Arcturus Defense Solutions for close-quarters urban pacification operations. Embedded within its reinforced knuckle array are sixteen independently actuated piezoelectric transducer nodes, each capable of generating a localized shear wave pulse timed to the moment of impact. When the fist connects with a surface — biological or structural — the system fires a cascading lateral stress fracture pattern into the target, multiplying the destructive potential of a single strike by propagating internal rupture along natural material fault lines rather than relying on raw kinetic energy alone.

What distinguishes the TSG-4 from simpler shock gauntlets is its onboard Fault Mapping Processor, a compact subsystem that reads surface impedance data through the fingertip contact pads during the half-second before a committed strike. This allows the weapon to modulate its shear frequency in real time — hardened ceramics, bone, composite armor, and biological tissue all receive individually tuned pulses optimized to their structural resonance. The result is a weapon that hits differently depending on what it hits, adapting like a surgeon's understanding of material science applied through a closed fist.

The gauntlet's external profile is deliberately understated: matte-black articulated plating over a gel-damping inner glove, with no visible emitters or power cells. Operators have noted that its subtlety is part of its psychological value — adversaries rarely recognize the weapon until after the first strike has already shattered something internal.
specifications:
weight: 1.4 kg (per gauntlet)
power source: Integrated microcell, 200 strike capacity per charge
shear frequency range: 800 Hz – 14 kHz adaptive
transducer nodes: 16
fault mapping latency: < 0.4 seconds pre-strike
armor compatibility: Fits over standard combat gloves up to 8mm composite
recharge time: 45 minutes via inductive pad
tactical_use: Operators use the TSG-4 in breach-and-clear scenarios where gunfire would compromise structural integrity or trigger acoustic sensors. Against armored targets, repeated strikes to the same location allow the Fault Mapping Processor to progressively deepen fracture networks, effectively softening armor before a finishing blow. In anti-cyborg applications, the shear pulse has demonstrated effectiveness at cracking housing around subdermal implants, causing secondary damage from fragment migration. Special forces units employ the gauntlets in pairs, coordinating simultaneous bilateral strikes to generate intersecting shear wave interference patterns capable of defeating materials resistant to unidirectional stress.
cultural_context: Within GLMZ's corporate security apparatus, the TSG-4 has become a quiet status symbol among close-protection details and executive enforcers — the kind of weapon that says its owner doesn't need to draw anything. Street-level fixers who acquire them through grey channels often have one gauntlet rather than a pair, a practical limitation that has ironically become a recognizable aesthetic. The nickname 'The Handshake' originated in the Kovač District after a mid-level trade negotiation ended with one party's lead representative hospitalized with seventeen internal fractures — the other party's representative was never charged, as no weapon was recovered.
known_users: Corporate enforcers operating under diplomatic immunity
Breach specialists in Tier 4 mercenary outfits
Underground pit fighters in the Sublevel circuits
'Gantry' Velasco, independent contractor and former ADS field tester
story_hooks: A prototype TSG-5 with an unlocked frequency ceiling has gone missing from an Arcturus R&D facility — it is capable of shear pulses that can fracture load-bearing columns, and someone is using it to systematically destabilize a rival corporation's headquarters building.

The players are hired to authenticate a pair of TSG-4s being sold at a black market auction — but the serial numbers trace back to a classified operation that Arcturus officially denies ever occurred.

A street doctor in the Sublevel circuits has been seeing a pattern of internal injuries consistent with TSG-4 use, all from victims who share one employer — she wants someone to find out who is wearing the gauntlet before her next patient doesn't survive.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, form-fitting combat gauntlet that merges the aesthetic of tactical gear with surgical precision. The silhouette is distinctly anthropomorphic — hugging the hand and forearm in articulated segments that suggest both protection and controlled lethality. At rest, it appears almost understated; in motion, the interlocking plates catch light in ways that hint at the technology beneath.
physical_description.dimensions: Gauntlet length: 32 cm (hand to mid-forearm). Knuckle plate array: 8 cm across. Palm width: 10 cm. Designed to fit standard adult hand frame.
physical_description.weight_description: Balanced and purposeful at 1.4 kg. The weight distribution favors the knuckles without creating wrist fatigue; operators report it feels like wearing a weighted glove rather than armor, responsive to natural hand movement.
physical_description.primary_material: Matte-black articulated titanium-composite plating over a gel-damping inner glove layer. The knuckle nodes are reinforced ceramic-polymer hybrid housing the piezoelectric transducers.
physical_description.finish: Deep matte black with a subtle brushed texture that resists reflective signature. Wear patterns typically show faint discoloration at impact zones from residual frequency harmonics. The plating edges have a satin finish.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: industrial matte black. Accent: minimal — faint phosphorescent blue traces along the articulation joints visible only under direct light, indicating power state.
physical_description.grip_texture: The inner glove is textured rubberized polymer with subtle radial grip pads on the palm. The knuckle plates are bare composite with microscopic finger-contact sensors — smooth but not slippery, designed for both bare skin and standard combat glove integration.
distinctive_features: Sixteen evenly-spaced raised knuckle nodes arranged in a double-row pattern, each approximately 0.8 cm in diameter
Fingertip contact pads: subtle circular indentations on each digit, visible only on close inspection
Minimal power indicator: thin phosphorescent line along the inner wrist edge that pulses faintly when charged
Articulated finger segments with concealed joint mechanics, allowing full dexterity
Heat vents as micro-perforations along the inner forearm edge, nearly invisible without magnification
Inductive charge port: recessed circular pad on the dorsal forearm, flush-mounted
Reinforced knuckle ridge with subtle serration for structural emphasis rather than cutting (purely aesthetic)
The gel-damping layer visible at seams and wrist opening, appearing as dark amber translucent material
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS logo embossed on the outer wrist plate in minimal serif lettering (2 cm wide). Serial designation 'TSG-4' laser-etched on the inductive pad housing. No visible wear numbers or operational markings — deliberately clean for field deployment.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field units show progressive discoloration at the knuckle nodes (faint dark rings) from repeated stress-mapping operations and microfracture residue. Well-maintained gauntlets retain the matte finish; heavily-used variants develop a worn sheen at impact points. Military exemplars are meticulous — gel layers are monitored and replaced per spec, power cells swapped at regulation intervals. Battle-scarred variants show cracked plating around the knuckle array and darkened surfaces from heat exposure during extended strike sequences.
